findings.title: A quote spanning a blank line is never found in its file
findings.why: `_squash` turns a blank or whitespace-only line into "", but the squashed parts are joined with a single space (`" ".join(parts)`), so every blank line leaves a run of two or more spaces in the searched text, while `_squash(quote)` can never contain a double space. A quote that is verbatim in the file but crosses a paragraph break therefore fails `.find`, the basis is marked "failed" with "the quote is not in <path>", the verifier is told the program could not confirm it, and quick mode drops the 🔴/🟡 finding entirely. The docstring's promise ("whitespace not counted") is not met; the PR/issue branches squash the whole text, so the same quote checks out there and fails here.

findings.title: A quote occurring twice is 'corrected' to its first occurrence, discarding correct lines
findings.why: `_find` returns the first match in the file, and when the model's cited range does not contain that first match the code assumes the lines are wrong and rewrites `source` to the first occurrence. If the rule is restated in the file (common in conventions/spec files), a model that cited the second, correct occurrence has its source replaced by an unrelated place; the basis is stored as "corrected", which `checked_out`/`supported` treat as confirmed, and `describe` tells the verifier "the files, lines and quote are there". The finding is then judged against code it does not describe, and in quick mode it is published on a fabricated location.

findings.title: Dropping `evidence` destroys the justification of every already-published finding
findings.why: The new column is added with `DEFAULT '[]'` and `evidence` is then dropped with no backfill, so every finding stored by an earlier run loses its reason permanently and comes back from the API as `basis: []`. Reviews already in the database (shown through the findings API and carried into later rounds) become unexplained, and the loss is irreversible. Also, `DROP COLUMN` aborts the migration (and hence startup) if anything in the existing schema - an index, view or trigger - still references `evidence`.
